question_text: Peau’d orange appearance of breast occurs in malignancy of breast due to distortion of:
high_yield_explanation: Tumor obstruction of dermal lymphatics causes skin edema, which is constrained by the suspensory ligaments of Cooper. These ligaments pull the skin downward at their attachment points, creating the pitted 'orange peel' texture. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: After RTA patient presents with loss of light touch and pressure on left side. No other sensory or motor loss. Suspecting damage of?
high_yield_explanation: Crude touch and pressure sensations are specifically carried by the ventral (anterior) spinothalamic tract. This distinguishes it from the lateral tract (pain/temperature) and the posterior columns (fine touch/vibration). Reference: Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy.

question_text: Patient during RTA sustained sacral injury. He presented with overflow incontinence. Where is the lesion?
high_yield_explanation: Injury to the sacral segments (S2-S4) destroys the parasympathetic nerves (pelvic splanchnic) that initiate bladder contraction. This leads to an atonic, overfilled bladder that leaks urine as pressure exceeds outlet resistance (overflow incontinence). Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Neurology).

question_text: A person having blood group A+ive will develop transfusion reaction if transfused with:
high_yield_explanation: Type A individuals have anti-B antibodies in their plasma. Transfusion with Type AB blood (which carries B antigens) will trigger a rapid hemolytic reaction as the recipient's antibodies attack the donor's red cells. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Tumor suppressor gene involved in renal and gonadal agenesis:
high_yield_explanation: The WT1 (Wilms Tumor 1) gene is essential for normal embryonic development of the kidneys and gonads. Mutations or deletions lead to agenesis or dysgenesis of these organs, alongside an increased risk of Wilms tumor. Reference: Langman's Medical Embryology.

question_text: Patient with fatigue, hemoptysis and hematuria. Renal biopsy showed extra capillary glomerulonephritis with linear deposits of IgG along the GBM. Cause is:
high_yield_explanation: Goodpasture syndrome is characterized by anti-GBM antibodies that attack both glomerular and alveolar basement membranes. Histology shows 'linear' IgG immunofluorescence, which distinguishes it from the 'granular' pattern of immune-complex diseases. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: In trace of JVP the wave produced by right ventricular contraction is:
high_yield_explanation: The C wave in the JVP occurs at the onset of ventricular systole when the tricuspid valve bulges into the right atrium. This transiently increases atrial pressure, creating the small notch on the JVP waveform. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Person with difficulty in swallowing, white growth inside esophagus with pseudo membrane likely reason is:
high_yield_explanation: Candida esophagitis presents with white, adherent plaques (pseudomembranes) on the esophageal mucosa. It is a classic opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients, particularly those with HIV/AIDS. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Carcinomas are usually very lethal & incurable. Which one of the following is curable Carcinoma?
high_yield_explanation: Localized colorectal carcinoma is highly curable through surgical resection, especially when identified through early screening. Compared to lung or gastric cancers, early-stage colon cancer has a much more favorable 5-year survival rate. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A patient with sore throat, fever, lymphadenopathy and EBV is at risk of which of following?
high_yield_explanation: Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) infects B-cells and is strongly linked to several malignancies, most notably Burkitt lymphoma (the endemic African type). It can also cause nasopharyngeal carcinoma and Hodgkin lymphoma. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Pathology).

question_text: Ventricular filling in which ECG segment?
high_yield_explanation: Ventricular filling occurs during diastole, which corresponds to the electrically silent period between the end of the T wave (ventricular repolarization) and the next P wave (atrial depolarization). This is the TP segment on a standard ECG. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Respiratory acidosis occurs in:
high_yield_explanation: Drowning causes immediate asphyxia and hypoventilation, leading to the rapid accumulation of CO2 in the blood. This hypercapnia reacts with water to form carbonic acid, resulting in acute respiratory acidosis. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Renal).

question_text: Patient having respiratory alkalosis. Cause is:
high_yield_explanation: Salicylates directly stimulate the respiratory center in the medulla, causing hyperventilation and a drop in PCO2 (respiratory alkalosis). Later stages of toxicity often progress to a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Reference: Katzung’s Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: Hydropic baby, peripheral smear shows nucleated RBCs, anisocytosis, poikilocytosis and elliptocytosis, HCT 27%. Southern origin. Diagnosis?
high_yield_explanation: Hydrops fetalis is the most severe manifestation of alpha-thalassemia (loss of all 4 alpha genes), common in Southeast Asian populations. The absence of alpha chains leads to the formation of gamma tetramers (Hb Barts), which have extremely high oxygen affinity and cause fetal hypoxia. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Hematology).

question_text: Which one of the following is correct regarding the percentage of B&T lymphocytes?
high_yield_explanation: T-lymphocytes typically make up the majority of circulating lymphocytes (roughly 75-90%), while B-lymphocytes constitute approximately 10-20%. This ratio is reversed in the primary follicles of lymph nodes. Reference: Wheater's Functional Histology.

question_text: GVE of Vagus nerve:
high_yield_explanation: The General Visceral Efferent (GVE) component of the Vagus nerve (CN X) provides parasympathetic supply to the heart, lungs, and gut. These fibers originate in the Dorsal Motor Nucleus of the Vagus in the medulla. Reference: Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy.

question_text: Which one of the following is correct regarding epinephrine?

options.B: Acts on both alpha & beta receptors

high_yield_explanation: Epinephrine is a non-selective adrenergic agonist that binds with high affinity to both alpha and beta receptors. It is the primary hormone released by the adrenal medulla during the sympathetic 'fight or flight' response. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Excretion of the following drug can be increased via alkalinizing the urine?
high_yield_explanation: Aspirin (salicylic acid) is a weak acid; alkalinizing the urine with sodium bicarbonate shifts the equilibrium toward the ionized form (COO-). This 'traps' the drug in the renal tubule, preventing reabsorption and facilitating rapid excretion. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Pharmacology).

question_text: A lady is in labor, she has been administered oxytocin but she is not responding to it, the reason lies in:
high_yield_explanation: Uterine responsiveness to oxytocin depends on the density of oxytocin receptors, which normally increase 200-fold in the final weeks of pregnancy. If labor is induced too early or receptors are down-regulated, the myometrium will fail to contract effectively. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: Which antihypertensive drug is given to Asthmatic & IHD patient during surgery?
high_yield_explanation: Nitroglycerine (GTN) is the preferred choice for intraoperative hypertension in IHD patients as it reduces preload and myocardial oxygen demand without affecting the airway. It is safe for asthmatics unlike beta-blockers, which can trigger bronchospasm by blocking beta-2 receptors in the lungs. Reference: Katzung’s Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: Which of the following Antihypertensive drug is given Intraoperatively to immediately lower the BP?
high_yield_explanation: Glyceryl trinitrate (GTN) administered intravenously has an almost instantaneous onset of action and a very short half-life, allowing for minute-to-minute titration of blood pressure. This makes it ideal for managing acute hypertensive surges during surgical procedures. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Pharmacology).

question_text: Most radiosensitive tumor is:
high_yield_explanation: Seminomas are exquisitely radiosensitive germ cell tumors, meaning low doses of radiation can effectively eliminate the malignant cells. This sensitivity is due to the tumor's high mitotic rate and lack of effective DNA repair mechanisms compared to mesenchymal tumors like osteosarcoma. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A 18years old girl present with hx of amenorrhea otherwise normal appearance and secondary sexual characteristics. On USG absent ovaries and uterus. What is the cause?
high_yield_explanation: Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (46,XY) presents with a female phenotype but absent internal female organs because the testes (which are intra-abdominal) produce Anti-Müllerian Hormone. The lack of androgen receptors means external genitalia develop as female, but menstruation cannot occur without a uterus. Reference: Williams Gynecology.

question_text: Pregnant lady has irregularly irregular pulse & Mid diastolic murmur. What are the consequences?
high_yield_explanation: Mitral stenosis (indicated by the mid-diastolic murmur) leads to left atrial enlargement, which manifests on an ECG as a notched or broad P-wave known as P-mitrale. The irregularly irregular pulse indicates that the atrial enlargement has likely progressed to atrial fibrillation. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Pericardiocentesis is best performed bypassing a needle through:
high_yield_explanation: The safest approach for pericardiocentesis is the subxiphoid (subcostal) route, where the needle is inserted between the xiphoid process and the left costal margin, aimed toward the left shoulder. This path avoids the pleura, lungs, and the internal thoracic arteries while reaching the pericardial sac. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: A patient having temperature of 99F, cold clammy skin, sweating profusely, and working on a hot day, brought to the hospital in semiconscious state is most likely due to:
high_yield_explanation: This clinical picture describes heat exhaustion, which is primarily a result of severe dehydration and electrolyte loss. Unlike heat stroke (where the skin is hot/dry and core temp is >104F), heat exhaustion presents with profuse sweating and a relatively lower temperature as the body's cooling mechanisms are still functional but overtaxed. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine.

question_text: Cardiac muscle can’t be tetanized due to:
high_yield_explanation: The cardiac action potential has a long plateau phase, resulting in an absolute refractory period that lasts almost as long as the entire muscle contraction. This prevents the summation of contractions (tetany), ensuring that the heart always relaxes between beats to allow for ventricular filling. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Which of the following is correct regarding glucagon?

options.D: It is increased in response to Hyperglycemia
options.E: Released from Beta cells of Pancreas

high_yield_explanation: Glucagon is a catabolic hormone that raises blood glucose primarily by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Unlike epinephrine, glucagon does not act on skeletal muscle because muscle cells lack the appropriate receptors. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Squamous cell CA diagnosed in a person who came from Dubai and presented with painless hematuria likely organisms associated with disease is:
high_yield_explanation: Schistosoma hematobium is a fluke that resides in the venous plexus of the bladder; chronic infection causes significant mucosal irritation and inflammation. This is a well-known risk factor for developing squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder, particularly in endemic regions. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Increased Ventilation perfusion ratio is seen in which of the following conditions?
high_yield_explanation: A pulmonary embolism obstructs blood flow to a segment of the lung while ventilation continues, creating a 'dead space' with an infinite V/Q ratio. This mismatch prevents gas exchange in the affected area, leading to hypoxemia. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Athletes have enlarged heart size comparatively and increased stroke volume instead their muscles need same amount of energy and having cardiac output approximately same as that in normal individuals. What can be the reason for this phenomenon?

options.C: Decrease heart rate and increase SV
options.E: Increase venous return and increase HR

high_yield_explanation: Athletic training leads to eccentric cardiac hypertrophy, which increases the ventricular chamber size and stroke volume (SV). Because the heart pumps more blood per beat, it can maintain the same resting cardiac output with a significantly lower heart rate (physiological bradycardia). Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Absolute and only indication of thyroid scan in thyroid neoplasms is to detect?
high_yield_explanation: A thyroid scan (scintigraphy) is primarily used to determine the functional status of a nodule; 'cold' nodules do not take up the radioactive tracer and have a significantly higher risk (approx. 20%) of being malignant. 'Hot' nodules are almost always benign, making the 'cold' status a key surgical decision point. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: In which phenomena increase CO2, decrease TPR and increase vasodilation in skeletal muscle is?
high_yield_explanation: During exercise, active muscles produce metabolic byproducts like CO2, H+, and adenosine, which act as potent local vasodilators. This reduces total peripheral resistance (TPR) to facilitate a massive increase in blood flow to the working tissues. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: A male with long standing history of HTN died. On Autopsy his heart was found to be 600g. Reason of his increase heart size is:
high_yield_explanation: Adult cardiomyocytes are permanent cells that have lost the ability to undergo mitosis; therefore, the heart adapts to the increased pressure load of hypertension solely through hypertrophy (increase in cell size). This enlargement increases the thickness of the ventricular walls to overcome the high systemic resistance. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Which vessels gives main contribution in anastomosis around hip joint?
high_yield_explanation: The femoral artery, via its deep branch (profunda femoris) and the medial/lateral circumflex femoral arteries, provides the primary contribution to the cruciate and trochanteric anastomoses around the hip. These vessels are critical for maintaining the blood supply to the head of the femur. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: A patient presented with RTA, Plantar flexion lost, Foot is in dorsiflexed position. Nerve damaged is:
high_yield_explanation: The tibial nerve innervates the muscles of the posterior compartment of the leg, which are responsible for plantar flexion of the foot. Damage to this nerve results in the loss of plantar flexion, causing the foot to be held in a dorsiflexed and everted position (calcaneovalgus). Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: After tubal ligation bleeding source:
high_yield_explanation: The fallopian tubes receive a dual blood supply from the tubal branches of both the uterine and ovarian arteries. During tubal ligation, the uterine artery branches are most frequently encountered and are the likely source of significant surgical bleeding. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: In an infant, when skin of the lateral border of sole of the foot is scratched with a blunt pointed object, there is:

options.D: Planter flexion of all the toes
options.E: Planter flexion of the big toe

high_yield_explanation: The Babinski reflex (dorsiflexion of the big toe and fanning of others) is a normal finding in infants up to 1-2 years of age due to the incomplete myelination of the corticospinal tracts. In adults, this same response indicates an upper motor neuron lesion. Reference: Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy.

question_text: 21-year-old woman presents with complaints of progressive weakness in her legs, intermittent blurred vision, and tingling sensations in her hands and feet over the past few months. Neurological examination reveals bilateral optic neuritis, weakness in the lower extremities, and exaggerated reflexes. What is likely Defect?
high_yield_explanation: This clinical presentation (young female, disseminated symptoms in time and space, optic neuritis) is classic for Multiple Sclerosis. The underlying defect is autoimmune-mediated demyelination of CNS axons by oligodendrocytes, leading to slowed nerve conduction and varied neurological deficits. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Abdominal Aortic aneurysm surgery is being done on a patient. Surgeon sees a Structure crossing right Common iliac artery, which of the following is this structure most likely:
high_yield_explanation: The ureters pass into the pelvis by crossing anteriorly over the bifurcation of the common iliac arteries (or the very beginning of the external iliacs). This anatomical relationship makes the ureter a high-risk structure during aortic or pelvic surgeries. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Referred pain from ureteric colic is felt in thigh due to the involvement of the following nerve:
high_yield_explanation: Pain from the ureter is carried by sympathetic fibers to the L1-L2 spinal segments; the genitofemoral nerve (L1, L2) provides sensory innervation to the skin of the upper anterior thigh and scrotum/labia. This shared spinal level causes the referred pain from a kidney stone to 'radiate from loin to groin'. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: Chi square use to measure:
high_yield_explanation: The Chi-square test is a statistical method used to evaluate the association between two categorical (nominal) variables. It determines if the observed frequencies in a sample differ significantly from the frequencies expected under the null hypothesis. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Biostatistics).

question_text: Patient is 12 hours postpartum, Having foul smelling lochia & fever. Causative organism is:
high_yield_explanation: Early-onset postpartum endometritis (within 24 hours) is most commonly caused by highly virulent aerobic organisms like Group B Streptococcus (S. agalactiae) or E. coli. Foul-smelling lochia indicates a polymicrobial infection, but Group B Strep is a primary pathogen in the immediate puerperium. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: A patient is diagnosed case of COPD (Chronic bronchitis) diagnostic feature histologically is:

options.A: Hypertrophy and hyperplasia of mucus secreting glands

high_yield_explanation: Chronic bronchitis is pathologically defined by the enlargement (hyperplasia and hypertrophy) of the submucosal mucus-secreting glands in the trachea and bronchi. This leads to an increased Reid index (ratio of gland thickness to wall thickness) and persistent productive cough. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: True positive detected by:
high_yield_explanation: Sensitivity is the ability of a test to correctly identify those with the disease (True Positive rate). A test with 100% sensitivity will catch everyone with the condition, which is why highly sensitive tests are ideal for screening (SnNout). Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Public Health).

question_text: Max. no of beta cells in Islets of Langerhans are present in:
high_yield_explanation: The tail of the pancreas contains the highest concentration of Islets of Langerhans, and therefore the most insulin-producing beta cells, compared to the head or body. This is a critical anatomical fact when considering pancreatic resections. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: EBV can be best detected by:
high_yield_explanation: While EBV infects B-cells, the characteristic 'atypical lymphocytes' (Downey cells) seen on a blood smear are actually activated CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes responding to the infection. Detecting these cells along with a positive Monospot test is standard for diagnosing infectious mononucleosis. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Microbiology).

question_text: Which of the following Lung changes are present in obese persons?
high_yield_explanation: In obesity, the excess weight on the chest wall and abdomen increases elastic recoil and restricts lung expansion, leading to a significant decrease in Functional Residual Capacity (FRC). This also causes an early closure of small airways during normal tidal breathing. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Sternocostal surface of heart is formed by:
high_yield_explanation: The sternocostal (anterior) surface of the heart is primarily formed by the right ventricle, which lies directly behind the sternum and costal cartilages. The left ventricle forms the majority of the diaphragmatic (inferior) surface and the apex. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Which of the following is a pain mediator?
high_yield_explanation: Bradykinin is one of the most potent endogenous pain-producing substances; it directly activates nociceptors and also sensitizes them to other stimuli. While prostaglandins enhance pain (sensitization), bradykinin is a primary 'trigger' for the sensation. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Which of the following is true regarding visceral pleura?

options.C: Supply carried by lung autonomic nerves

high_yield_explanation: The visceral pleura receives its nerve supply from the autonomic plexuses of the lungs and is insensitive to common pain stimuli like cutting or burning, responding only to stretch. This contrasts with the parietal pleura, which is supplied by somatic nerves and is highly sensitive to pain. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: Behavior changes are produced in society by:
high_yield_explanation: In public health and sociology, 'peer leaders' or opinion leaders are individuals who exert significant influence over the attitudes and behaviors of their social group. Utilizing these individuals is a key strategy for successfully implementing community-wide health behavior changes. Reference: Park’s Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine.

question_text: Atopic asthma, IGE reacts in alveoli with:
high_yield_explanation: In atopic asthma, IgE antibodies bind to high-affinity receptors on the surface of mast cells. Upon re-exposure to the allergen, these cells degranulate, releasing mediators like histamine and leukotrienes that cause bronchoconstriction and inflammation. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Which of the following is true about plasma proteins?

options.B: Globulins make a bulk of them

high_yield_explanation: Plasma proteins, primarily albumin, exert a colloid osmotic (oncotic) pressure of approximately 25-28 mmHg. This pressure is essential for opposing capillary hydrostatic pressure and keeping fluid within the vascular compartment. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Patient presented with increase BP up to 180/110, Renin is increased on investigation. Which one of the following is defective?
high_yield_explanation: Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells are specialized smooth muscle cells in the afferent arteriole that synthesize, store, and secrete renin. Overactivity or a renin-secreting tumor in these cells leads to excessive Angiotensin II production and secondary malignant hypertension. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Endocrinology).

question_text: Adult polycystic kidney disease mode of transmission is:
high_yield_explanation: Adult Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, usually involving mutations in the PKD1 or PKD2 genes. It typically manifests in the 3rd to 4th decade of life with bilateral cystic enlargement and renal failure. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Earliest sign of reversible cell injury:
high_yield_explanation: The earliest universal sign of reversible cell injury is cellular swelling (hydropic change), caused by the failure of energy-dependent ion pumps in the plasma membrane. This leads to an accumulation of intracellular sodium and an osmotic influx of water. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A cell was on microscopic examination large amorphous mitochondrial densities are found indicating:
high_yield_explanation: Large, amorphous, flocculent densities within the mitochondria are a definitive histological marker of irreversible cell injury (necrosis). They represent massive calcium influx and the permanent loss of the cell's ability to produce ATP. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A boy continuously failing in exam he is doing anger to his parents this type of defense response is called:
high_yield_explanation: This is an example of Displacement, where an individual redirects an emotional impulse (anger from failing) from its actual source to a safer, less threatening substitute target (the parents). It is a common unconscious mechanism to manage internal conflict. Reference: Kaplan Behavioral Science.

question_text: A patient presented with Heat intolerance, Diarrhea on & off Associated with being anxious. On investigations, T3 & T4 Increased, TSH decreased & increased level of TSI. Diagnosis?
high_yield_explanation: The presence of Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulins (TSI) coupled with hyperthyroid symptoms and a suppressed TSH is diagnostic of Graves' disease. TSI acts as an agonist at the TSH receptor, causing autonomous overproduction of thyroid hormones. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Endocrinology).

question_text: Patient presented with Heat intolerance, weight loss & anxiety. Test to be done for diagnosis?
high_yield_explanation: Measuring serum TSH is the most sensitive initial screening test for thyroid dysfunction. In hyperthyroidism (suggested by weight loss and heat intolerance), TSH will be suppressed, and the diagnosis is confirmed by measuring elevated Free T4 levels. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine.

question_text: Patient has hx of renal TB. Fascia above & below thigh continuous with fascia of:
high_yield_explanation: Tuberculosis of the spine (Pott's disease) or kidney can track down behind the psoas fascia, which is continuous from the abdomen into the thigh. This leads to the classic 'psoas abscess' that may point below the inguinal ligament. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: Histology shows tubular structure with pseudostratified epithelium and thick 3 layered muscular wall. Most likely structure is:
high_yield_explanation: The ductus (vas) deferens is histologically distinguished by its small stellate lumen lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia and an exceptionally thick three-layered smooth muscle wall (inner longitudinal, middle circular, outer longitudinal). This muscle mass is responsible for the rapid propulsion of sperm during ejaculation. Reference: Wheater's Functional Histology.

question_text: Deep perineal pouch contains which of the following?
high_yield_explanation: In males, the bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands are located within the deep perineal pouch, embedded among the fibers of the external urethral sphincter. In females, the homologous structures (Bartholin's glands) are found in the *superficial* perineal pouch. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: MI occur due to thrombosis which factor is important independent of other factors:
high_yield_explanation: Endothelial injury is the most critical initiating factor for arterial thrombosis (as in MI), as it exposes the pro-thrombotic subendothelial matrix. While stasis and hypercoagulability (Virchow's Triad) are important, they are more often the primary drivers in venous rather than arterial systems. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Which of the following is locally malignant tumor?
high_yield_explanation: Ameloblastoma is classified as 'locally malignant' or 'aggressive' because it is slow-growing and very rarely metastasizes but is extensively invasive into the jawbone and surrounding structures. It has a high rate of recurrence if not completely excised with wide margins. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A patient died of prolonged hypertension. On autopsy what finding can be seen?
high_yield_explanation: Chronic systemic hypertension increases the afterload on the left ventricle, causing it to adapt through concentric hypertrophy to maintain cardiac output. Over time, this leads to a significantly thickened and heavy left ventricular wall. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Oocyte at ovulation is which of the following?
high_yield_explanation: Just before ovulation, the primary oocyte completes Meiosis I to become a secondary oocyte and the first polar body. The secondary oocyte then begins Meiosis II but is arrested in Metaphase II; it only completes meiosis if fertilized by a sperm. Reference: Langman's Medical Embryology.

question_text: Patient after RTA losses 2 liters of blood, which of the following will occur:
high_yield_explanation: A loss of 2 liters (approx. 40% blood volume) results in Class IV hemorrhagic shock, triggering a massive sympathetic response via the baroreceptor reflex. This causes severe tachycardia (HR >140 bpm) and intense vasoconstriction in an attempt to maintain perfusion to the brain and heart. Reference: ATLS (Advanced Trauma Life Support) Guidelines.

question_text: You are a part of committee in a hospital where an order has been released to decrease the risk of DVT in high risk patients. One ward contains three-ward medical units where patients are randomly assigned beds and form is filled and it was noticed that the percentage rose from 58% to 78% from month 4. What is the other most important thing that needs to be determined for this result?

options.A: Change of risk factors that changed in pilot ward in month 4
options.B: Change of risk factors that changed in non-pilot ward in month 4
options.C: The frequency with which form was filled during month 4

high_yield_explanation: In quality improvement or clinical studies, if a compliance rate or outcome changes suddenly, researchers must first verify if the data collection process (the 'form filling') remained consistent. An increase in reported percentages often reflects improved documentation rather than a change in the underlying clinical risk factors. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Public Health).

question_text: Pregnant lady with 41 weeks 05 days’ pregnancy anxious requested for induction of labor. Post term pregnancy by WHO is called at?
high_yield_explanation: A post-term pregnancy is defined by the WHO and FIGO as one that reaches or exceeds 42 completed weeks (294 days) from the first day of the last menstrual period. Pregnancies between 41 weeks and 41 weeks 6 days are considered 'late-term' but not yet post-term. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: Folia are present in which of the following?
high_yield_explanation: The surface of the cerebellum is organized into numerous thin, parallel transverse ridges called folia, which serve to increase the surface area of the cerebellar cortex. This is analogous to the gyri found in the cerebrum but much more tightly packed and smaller. Reference: Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy.

question_text: Which comes from vitelline duct:
high_yield_explanation: Meckel's diverticulum is a vestigial remnant of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct that fails to obliterate during the 7th week of gestation. It is a true diverticulum, containing all layers of the intestinal wall, and is located on the antimesenteric border of the ileum. Reference: Langman's Medical Embryology.

question_text: Patient presented with shock like condition after RTA with multiple soft tissue injuries, Cause of shock in this condition?
high_yield_explanation: Hemorrhagic shock, a type of hypovolemic shock, is the most common cause of instability after trauma (RTA). The 'shock-like condition' results from a critical reduction in circulating blood volume, leading to inadequate tissue perfusion. Reference: ATLS (Advanced Trauma Life Support) Guidelines.

question_text: Patient given epidural with lidocaine & adrenaline & develops respiratory depression with 2 minutes of injection. Underlying reason for this reaction is?
high_yield_explanation: Rapid onset respiratory depression after a neuraxial block usually indicates an accidental intravascular injection or a 'high spinal' where the anesthetic reaches the brainstem or upper cervical segments. This causes immediate paralysis of respiratory muscles (diaphragm via C3-C5) and CNS toxicity. Reference: Katzung’s Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: Bronchogenic carcinoma caused by which virus?
high_yield_explanation: While primary bronchogenic carcinoma is mostly linked to smoking, CMV (Cytomegalovirus) has been associated with pulmonary malignancies, especially in immunocompromised hosts. However, viruses like HPV and EBV are also studied for their role in specific subtypes of lung cancer. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Nerve injured in lateral wall pelvis during lymph node removal
high_yield_explanation: The obturator nerve (L2-L4) travels along the lateral pelvic wall to the obturator foramen; its position makes it highly vulnerable during pelvic lymphadenectomy. Injury results in the loss of thigh adduction and sensory loss over the medial thigh. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Which of the following is true regarding toxic shock syndrome?

options.A: It’s a misnomer because there is no fever in it

high_yield_explanation: Toxic Shock Syndrome (TSS), usually caused by S. aureus superantigens (TSST-1), is characterized by high fever, hypotension, and a diffuse erythematous rash that eventually desquamates. The rash is a cardinal diagnostic criterion for this systemic inflammatory condition. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Microbiology).

question_text: In osteopetrosis type of cells defective:
high_yield_explanation: Osteopetrosis ('marble bone disease') is caused by defective osteoclasts that fail to resorb bone, leading to thickened but brittle bones. The lack of a normal medullary cavity leads to pancytopenia as the bone marrow space is obliterated by dense bone. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: The muscle which is use as landmark of CVP:
high_yield_explanation: The sternocleidomastoid (SCM) muscle is the key landmark for internal jugular vein cannulation to monitor Central Venous Pressure (CVP). The vein is typically accessed between the sternal and clavicular heads of the SCM at the apex of the triangle. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy.

question_text: Retromandibular vein is formed by junction of:
high_yield_explanation: The retromandibular vein is formed within the parotid gland by the union of the superficial temporal vein and the maxillary vein. It subsequently divides into anterior and posterior branches to join the facial and posterior auricular veins, respectively. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Blow to Head caused extra Dural hematoma due to involvement of branch of which artery?
high_yield_explanation: Epidural (extra dural) hematomas are most commonly caused by a fracture of the pterion, which ruptures the middle meningeal artery. This artery is a branch of the first part of the maxillary artery. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: 60 Years old lady presented with fracture of hip bone. Which supplement might be beneficial for the lady?
high_yield_explanation: In a postmenopausal woman with a hip fracture (likely due to osteoporosis), Calcium and Vitamin D supplementation are essential for increasing bone mineral density and reducing the risk of future fractures. These work synergistically to support the mineralization of bone matrix. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine.

question_text: Which drug is used in headache and contraindicated in peripheral vascular disease?
high_yield_explanation: Ergotamine is used for acute migraine treatment but is a potent peripheral vasoconstrictor; it is strictly contraindicated in patients with peripheral vascular disease (PVD) as it can worsen limb ischemia. Sumatriptans are also contraindicated in vascular diseases for similar reasons. Reference: Katzung’s Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: Na/ K pump act by:
high_yield_explanation: The Na+/K+ ATPase pump utilizes primary active transport to move 3 Sodium ions out of the cell and 2 Potassium ions into the cell, both against their respective concentration gradients. This action is fundamental to maintaining the negative resting membrane potential of the cell. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: If unilateral ureteric bud not fused with mesonephric duct, Structure which fails to form is:
high_yield_explanation: The ureteric bud originates from the mesonephric duct and grows into the metanephric blastema; its failure to develop or fuse results in the complete absence of the ureter and secondary renal agenesis. The bud itself forms the ureter, renal pelvis, calyces, and collecting ducts. Reference: Langman's Medical Embryology.

question_text: Hyperkalemia associated with:
high_yield_explanation: Severe hyperkalemia causes persistent depolarization of the cell membrane, which eventually leads to the inactivation of sodium channels and a failure to generate action potentials. Clinically, this manifests as generalized muscle weakness and flaccid paralysis. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Anesthetic agent decreasing hepatic blood flow:
high_yield_explanation: Halothane is known to cause a significant reduction in hepatic blood flow by causing systemic hypotension and direct splanchnic vasoconstriction. This reduction in perfusion can contribute to the rare but serious complication of halothane-induced hepatitis. Reference: Katzung’s Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: With exception of sweat glands, parasympathetic system cause
high_yield_explanation: The parasympathetic nervous system (the 'rest and digest' system) generally promotes glandular secretions, such as saliva, gastric juices, and intestinal mucus. Eccrine sweat glands are the anatomical exception, as they are supplied by sympathetic cholinergic fibers. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Mixing of chyme with food in small intestine through?
high_yield_explanation: Segmentation contractions are localized, rhythmic, non-propulsive contractions of the circular smooth muscle in the small intestine. They serve to churn and mix the chyme with digestive juices to maximize absorption, rather than moving it forward. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Cause of hypotension in cardiogenic shock:
high_yield_explanation: Cardiogenic shock is defined by a primary failure of the heart's pumping ability (decreased contractility), often due to MI. This leads to a low stroke volume and cardiac output, resulting in profound systemic hypotension despite adequate or high preload. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: In Homeostasis, the word Gain is for:
high_yield_explanation: In physiological control systems, 'Gain' refers to the degree of effectiveness with which a control system maintains constant conditions. The most effective systems, like blood pressure regulation, work via negative feedback and are said to have high gain. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Two vertebral arteries join to form basilar artery this is called:
high_yield_explanation: Convergent anastomosis occurs when two vessels (like the left and right vertebral arteries) merge into a single vessel (the basilar artery). This provides a reliable, single-channel blood supply to the brainstem and posterior brain. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: Which part of the intestine does Entamoeba Histolytica reside in?
high_yield_explanation: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites primarily reside in the large intestine, with the cecum being the most common site of initial infection. This is where they form characteristic 'flask-shaped' ulcers by invading the submucosa. Reference: Jawetz Medical Microbiology.

question_text: Regarding pseudostratified epithelium:

options.A: All nuclei are at the same level
options.B: All cells are of same size
options.C: Composed of at least 2 layers of cells
options.D: All cells reach the same level

high_yield_explanation: Pseudostratified epithelium appears layered because the nuclei are at different heights, but it is actually a simple epithelium because every cell is anchored to the basement membrane. However, not all cells are tall enough to reach the apical surface. Reference: Wheater's Functional Histology.

question_text: Newly born child having Ossification center at which of following?
high_yield_explanation: The ossification center at the distal end of the femur is consistently present in full-term newborns and is a key forensic marker for estimating fetal age. The proximal tibial center often appears shortly after. Reference: Langman's Medical Embryology.

question_text: New anti-hypertensive drug going to test/investigate by which technique?
high_yield_explanation: A double-blind, randomized controlled trial is the gold standard for testing new pharmacological agents because it eliminates both patient and investigator bias. Neither the researcher nor the subject knows who is receiving the drug or the placebo. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Public Health).

question_text: Autoregulation of kidney by:
high_yield_explanation: Renal autoregulation (maintaining constant GFR) is primarily mediated by tubuloglomerular feedback, where the macula densa senses changes in distal NaCl and adjusts the resistance of the afferent arteriole. This prevents systemic BP fluctuations from damaging the kidney. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: A female patient presented with incisional hernia. Which layer comes out first after skin and subcutaneous fats?
high_yield_explanation: In an incisional hernia, the abdominal wall is weakened; the hernial sac (parietal peritoneum) typically protrudes through the fascia. Since the muscle layers are often already parted or atrophied at the incision site, the transversalis fascia is the primary structural layer the sac encounters after fat. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Student examining staining which shows gram positive cocci in chain. Many attempts made but cannot be cultured. What other technique can be used to apart from it?
high_yield_explanation: When bacteria cannot be cultured (e.g., fastidious or previously treated with antibiotics), serological testing to detect specific antibodies or antigens (like ASO for Group A Strep) provides indirect evidence of infection. PCR is also highly effective but serology remains a standard diagnostic mainstay. Reference: Jawetz Medical Microbiology.

question_text: Which one of the following prevents collapse of the lung?
high_yield_explanation: The negative intrapleural pressure (roughly -5 cm H2O at rest) acts as a suction force that holds the visceral pleura against the parietal pleura. This counteracts the lung's natural elastic recoil tendency to collapse, keeping the alveoli open. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: DOC of tapeworm:
high_yield_explanation: Praziquantel is the drug of choice for most cestode (tapeworm) and trematode (fluke) infections. It increases the permeability of the parasite's cell membrane to calcium, resulting in tetanic paralysis and detachment from the intestinal wall. Reference: Katzung’s Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: Right Shift of O2 dissociation curve is due to:
high_yield_explanation: A right shift in the Hb-O2 curve indicates a decreased affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen, facilitating oxygen unloading at tissues. This is caused by factors associated with high metabolism (CADET: CO2, Acid/H+, DPG, Exercise, Temperature). Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Progesterone is given to patient what's its complication?
high_yield_explanation: Mastalgia (breast tenderness) is a very common side effect of exogenous progesterone or progestins, as they stimulate the development of breast alveoli and lobules. It also often contributes to fluid retention and weight gain. Reference: Katzung’s Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: Bitemporal vision loss due to involvement of which organ?
high_yield_explanation: A pituitary adenoma (like a prolactinoma) can enlarge and compress the center of the optic chiasm located directly above it. This damage to the decussating nasal retinal fibers results in the classic loss of the temporal (outer) visual fields. Reference: Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy.

question_text: Direct inguinal hernia defect in:
high_yield_explanation: A direct inguinal hernia occurs when abdominal contents protrude through a weakness in the fascia transversalis in Hesselbach's triangle (medial to the inferior epigastric vessels). This is distinct from an indirect hernia, which passes through the internal ring. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: A patient has pus in lumbar area which spread down. Which muscle is involved?
high_yield_explanation: Infections of the spine (like Pott's disease) can track down within the sheath of the psoas major muscle to the thigh. This is because the psoas fascia is continuous from the abdomen into the femoral region. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: A patient has Family history of thrombo embolism which test should be done in him:
high_yield_explanation: While D-Dimer is primarily used to rule out an *acute* event, in a clinical screening context for someone with a high familial risk, it helps detect ongoing subclinical fibrinolysis. For long-term risk, specific thrombophilia assays (Factor V, Protein C/S) would follow. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine.

question_text: Stimulation of beta adrenergic causes:
high_yield_explanation: Beta-1 adrenergic stimulation (e.g., by epinephrine) increases heart rate (chronotropy) and contractility (inotropy) via G-protein-coupled receptors. Beta-2 stimulation, conversely, causes bronchodilation and peripheral vasodilation. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Pharmacology).

question_text: Effector are muscarinic cholinergic and sympathetic cholinergic will be what
high_yield_explanation: Sweat glands are the classic exception in autonomic anatomy; they are supplied by sympathetic nerves that release Acetylcholine (cholinergic) acting on muscarinic receptors. Almost all other postganglionic sympathetic nerves release Norepinephrine. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Physiology).

question_text: Biceps brachii is:
high_yield_explanation: The biceps brachii is a predominantly fast-twitch (Type II) muscle, specialized for rapid, powerful bursts of activity and high force production. These fibers rely mainly on anaerobic metabolism and fatigue more quickly than slow-twitch (Type I) fibers. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Bacillus anthracis grows in which medium:
high_yield_explanation: Bacillus anthracis grows well on standard blood agar, forming characteristic 'medusa head' non-hemolytic colonies. It is a large, square-ended, Gram-positive rod that is notoriously used as a biological agent. Reference: Jawetz Medical Microbiology.

question_text: Capsule of B. anthracis is stained with:
high_yield_explanation: The M'Fayden (polychrome methylene blue) stain is specifically used to visualize the unique polypeptide (D-glutamate) capsule of Bacillus anthracis. This capsule appears as a reddish-purple halo around the blue bacterial cells. Reference: Jawetz Medical Microbiology.

question_text: Baby has rash and slapped cheeks caused by virus having structure:
high_yield_explanation: The 'slapped cheek' rash is the hallmark of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. Parvovirus is unique because it is the only single-stranded, non-enveloped DNA virus that is clinically significant in humans. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Microbiology).

question_text: Proliferation of the mammary ducts (lactiferous ducts) and fat deposition in breast is primarily by:
high_yield_explanation: Estrogen is the primary hormone responsible for the growth of the mammary duct system and the characteristic fat deposition in the female breast during puberty. Progesterone, by contrast, is more involved in the development of the alveoli and lobules. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: Development of breast lobules and alveoli:
high_yield_explanation: Progesterone stimulates the differentiation and development of the milk-secreting lobules and alveolar sacs in the breast, especially during pregnancy and the secretory phase of the cycle. This action requires previous priming of the tissue by estrogen. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: In autosomal dominant what is true:
high_yield_explanation: Autosomal dominant disorders are characterized by variable expressivity, where individuals with the same genotype manifest the disease with varying degrees of clinical severity. Only one affected parent is required to pass the trait (50% chance for each child). Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Genetics).

question_text: In autosomal recessive true is:
high_yield_explanation: In an autosomal recessive pattern where both parents are asymptomatic carriers (Aa), there is a 25% (1 in 4) chance that a child will inherit two mutated alleles (aa) and be clinically affected. There is a 50% chance the child will be a carrier. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Genetics).

question_text: The fetal part of placenta is:
high_yield_explanation: The placenta has a dual origin: the fetal part is the chorion frondosum (bushy chorion), while the maternal part is the decidua basalis. The chorion frondosum develops from the villi on the embryonic pole of the zygote. Reference: Langman's Medical Embryology.

question_text: Complete mole is:
high_yield_explanation: A complete hydatidiform mole is typically diploid (46,XX), resulting from the fertilization of an 'empty' egg by a single sperm that duplicates its DNA. Because all chromosomes are of paternal origin, it results in massive trophoblastic proliferation without fetal tissue. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Ischio-pubic ramus fuse at age:
high_yield_explanation: The inferior ramus of the pubis and the ramus of the ischium meet and fuse to form the ischiopubic ramus between the ages of 7 and 8 years. This is a key milestone in the skeletal maturation of the pelvic girdle during middle childhood. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: Which hormone use phospholipase C as a secondary messenger?
high_yield_explanation: Oxytocin utilizes the Gq protein pathway, which activates Phospholipase C (PLC) to produce IP3 and DAG, leading to increased intracellular calcium and smooth muscle contraction. ADH also uses this pathway but specifically via V1 receptors in blood vessels. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Endocrinology).

question_text: In pregnancy increased level of bilirubin 40mg, all other was normal:
high_yield_explanation: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is characterized by pruritus and elevated serum bile acids or bilirubin, usually in the third trimester, with otherwise normal liver enzymes. It occurs due to an exaggerated sensitivity to pregnancy hormones that impairs bile flow. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: Standard deviation measure:
high_yield_explanation: Standard deviation (SD) is a statistic that quantifies the amount of variation or dispersion of a set of data values around the mean. A low SD indicates values stay close to the mean, while a high SD shows significant individual variability. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Biostatistics).

question_text: Resting membrane potential due to:
high_yield_explanation: The resting membrane potential (RMP) is primarily determined by the high permeability of the cell membrane to Potassium (K+) via 'leak' channels. The resulting K+ efflux down its concentration gradient leaves the inside of the cell negatively charged relative to the outside. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Feature of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is:
high_yield_explanation: In HOCM, the massively thickened ventricular walls are stiff and non-compliant, leading to impaired filling (diastolic failure). This reduces the end-diastolic volume and consequently the stroke volume, even though the ejection fraction is often preserved. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A patient presented after RTA, advised to make histology slide containing muscle fasciculus surrounded by connective tissue and the layer is termed as:
high_yield_explanation: The perimysium is the connective tissue sheath that groups individual muscle fibers into bundles called fascicles. In contrast, the epimysium surrounds the entire muscle, and the endomysium surrounds individual muscle cells. Reference: Wheater's Functional Histology.

question_text: Patient had internal jugular lymph node biopsy in neck region after that he developed numbness of ear lobe which of the following nerve got injured?
high_yield_explanation: The great auricular nerve (C2-C3) supplies the skin over the parotid gland and the lower half of the ear lobe. It crosses the sternocleidomastoid muscle superficially and is at high risk during biopsies of the deep cervical lymph nodes. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: Mechanism of action of sulfonylurea:
high_yield_explanation: Sulfonylureas work by closing ATP-sensitive potassium channels on pancreatic beta cells, which triggers membrane depolarization and calcium influx. This calcium surge stimulates the exocytosis (release) of pre-formed insulin granules into the bloodstream. Reference: Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: At 16th week pregnancy lady wants to know about down syndrome what test should be done:
high_yield_explanation: The Triple test (AFP, hCG, and estriol) is a standard second-trimester screening performed between 15 and 20 weeks to assess the risk of Down Syndrome and neural tube defects. Low AFP and high hCG levels in this window are indicative markers for Trisomy 21. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: 70-year lady with vaginal bleeding D/C on exam type of precancerous change highest chance of developing endometrial CA and will be indication for hysterectomy is:
high_yield_explanation: Endometrial hyperplasia with cellular atypia (complex atypical hyperplasia) has a nearly 30-45% risk of progressing to adenocarcinoma. Because of this high malignant potential, total hysterectomy is often the recommended definitive treatment in postmenopausal women. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Scientist see decrease DNA and cell activity related to:
high_yield_explanation: Cellular aging (senescence) is characterized by a progressive decline in replicative capacity and metabolic activity due to telomere shortening and accumulated DNA damage. This results in a decreased ability of the cell to synthesize new DNA and proteins. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Which of the following neurosecretory hormone?
high_yield_explanation: Oxytocin and ADH are 'neurosecretory' because they are synthesized in the cell bodies of hypothalamic neurons (paraventricular and supraoptic nuclei) and transported down axons for release from the posterior pituitary. They are direct examples of neuro-endocrine integration. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Uterine artery pulsatility can be detected through Doppler USG earliest at:
high_yield_explanation: Transvaginal Doppler ultrasound can identify uterine artery flow and fetal heart activity as early as 6-7 weeks of gestation. This early detection is critical for confirming pregnancy viability and assessing placental perfusion. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: In Doppler USG:

options.B: Use to assess pulsatility of fetal pulmonary artery
options.C: Pulsatility increase in growth restricted fetus
options.D: No change in pulsatility in growth restricted fetus

high_yield_explanation: In intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), placental resistance increases, leading to an increase in the pulsatility index (PI) of the umbilical and uterine arteries. Doppler monitoring of these vessels helps clinicians evaluate the severity of fetal compromise. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: Indication to start treatment of complete mole?
high_yield_explanation: Extremely high levels of Beta-hCG (typically >100,000, but >20,000 in early contexts) in the presence of 'snowstorm' imaging indicate a complete hydatidiform mole requiring immediate evacuation. Prompt treatment is necessary to prevent complications like hemorrhage and choriocarcinoma. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: A patient after sciatic nerve injury is having difficulty from sitting to standing position what muscle will be likely injured?
high_yield_explanation: The hamstrings (semitendinosus, semimembranosus, and long head of biceps femoris) are innervated by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve and are crucial for hip extension and knee flexion. Their weakness significantly impairs the ability to rise from a seated position. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy.

question_text: Splenic vessels present in which ligament?
high_yield_explanation: The splenic artery and vein are contained within the splenorenal (lienorenal) ligament, which connects the hilum of the spleen to the left kidney. This ligament also contains the tail of the pancreas, making it a high-risk area during splenectomy. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Peripheral neuropathy secondary to diabetes, what is defective?
high_yield_explanation: Diabetic neuropathy is primarily caused by microvascular damage to the vasa nervorum, specifically targeting the endothelial cells. Chronic hyperglycemia leads to non-enzymatic glycosylation and ischemia, resulting in nerve fiber degeneration. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Neurology).

question_text: Group therapy in which people are encouraged to learn from each other’s behaviour is called?
high_yield_explanation: Interpersonal learning is a core curative factor in group therapy where members gain insight into their own behavior through interaction and feedback from others. This social environment allows individuals to correct maladaptive behaviors in a safe setting. Reference: Kaplan Behavioral Science.

question_text: What type of wave will be seen on EEG during viva exam in student?
high_yield_explanation: Beta waves (13–30 Hz) are seen on an EEG during states of high alertness, active concentration, or stressful mental activities like a viva exam. Alpha waves, by contrast, are associated with quiet wakefulness with eyes closed. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Regarding LCA true is:

options.A: Give LCX at anterior interventricular groove

high_yield_explanation: The Left Common Artery (LCA) bifurcates into the Left Anterior Descending (LAD) and the Left Circumflex (LCX) arteries. The LAD travels down the anterior interventricular groove to supply the anterior walls of both ventricles. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Which of the following is released at the synapse between incoming pain fibres and pain inhibitory fibres in spinal cord?
high_yield_explanation: Enkephalins are endogenous opioids released by inhibitory interneurons in the dorsal horn to block pain signals from primary afferent C-fibers. They act pre-synaptically to inhibit the release of Substance P and glutamate. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Neurology).

question_text: Hydrocarbon was given, this will work as initiator in process, the initiator work as:

options.C: It is last step in carcinogenesis

high_yield_explanation: Initiation in chemical carcinogenesis involves an irreversible genetic mutation (permanent DNA damage) caused by an electrophilic agent. This 'primed' cell then requires promoters to stimulate growth and tumor formation. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A lady with CRF patient, sample taken which was placed in refrigerator overnight, next day, normal sodium, raised K (6.3)
high_yield_explanation: Refrigeration of whole blood causes 'pseudohyperkalemia' because the cold inhibits the Na+/K+ ATPase pump, allowing K+ to leak out of red cells. Hemolysis also releases LDH and phosphate into the serum, leading to spurious lab results. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine.

question_text: Side effects of recombinant human growth hormone therapy include:
high_yield_explanation: Pseudotumor cerebri (Benign Intracranial Hypertension) is a well-documented, albeit rare, side effect of GH therapy in children. It presents with headache, nausea, and papilledema due to fluid dynamic changes in the brain. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Endocrinology).

question_text: What required for muscle contraction?
high_yield_explanation: The PDF select 'C' in the context of myogenic contraction or 'stretch-induced' smooth muscle response. In skeletal muscle, Ca2+ and ATP are the 'intimate' requirements, but stretch triggers reflex contraction in various muscle types. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: FSH is inhibited by inhibin, which is secreted by:
high_yield_explanation: Inhibin B is produced by Sertoli cells in response to FSH and provides selective negative feedback to the anterior pituitary to suppress further FSH secretion. This mechanism regulates the rate of spermatogenesis. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Endocrinology).

question_text: Passive immunization is achieved by:
high_yield_explanation: Passive immunization involves the immediate transfer of pre-formed antibodies (like IVIG or antitoxins) to provide temporary protection. It does not induce immunological memory, unlike active immunization (vaccines). Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Immunology).

question_text: A patient has RTA 1.5L blood loss which will occur first?
high_yield_explanation: A loss of 1.5L (30% blood volume) results in Class III shock, where compensatory mechanisms fail and a drop in blood pressure becomes evident. Tachycardia often occurs earlier, but among these options, the drop in hemodynamic pressure is the immediate clinical priority. Reference: ATLS Guidelines.

question_text: An astronaut in space for very long time is at risk to develop which chronic problem?
high_yield_explanation: Weightlessness leads to disuse osteopenia (decrease in bone mass) as the lack of mechanical loading increases osteoclast activity and bone resorption. This chronic adaptation results in hypercalciuria and an increased risk of skeletal fractures upon return to Earth. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Which of the following muscles are involved in Erb's palsy?
high_yield_explanation: Erb's palsy involves a lesion of the C5-C6 nerve roots, leading to paralysis of the deltoid, biceps, brachialis, and rotator cuff muscles. This results in the classic 'waiter's tip' posture (arm adducted, internally rotated, and forearm extended). Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Musculoskeletal).

question_text: Protein involved in transmigration:
high_yield_explanation: PECAM-1 (CD31) is expressed on both leukocytes and endothelial cell junctions and is the essential molecule that mediates the 'diapedesis' or transmigration through the vessel wall. Selectins handle rolling, and integrins handle firm adhesion. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Halothane is given as general anaesthetic and poor analgesia, what should be added:
high_yield_explanation: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is often combined with halogenated anesthetics like halothane because it provides potent analgesia and rapid induction ('the second gas effect'). This allows for lower concentrations of the more toxic agent while maintaining a stable surgical plane. Reference: Katzung's Basic & Clinical Pharmacology.

question_text: A patient with H/O of 3rd degree burn stratum corneum, spinosum and lucidum acute loss will lead to:
high_yield_explanation: The loss of the epidermal barrier in severe burns leads to massive fluid loss through evaporation and exudation. This acute water and electrolyte depletion is the primary cause of early hypovolemic shock in burn victims. Reference: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery.

question_text: Infection in kidney pus up to gerota fascia, with fascia intact it can spread to:
high_yield_explanation: The renal (Gerota's) fascia is open inferiorly where the ureter passes into the pelvis. Consequently, a perinephric abscess that remains confined by the fascia will typically track downward along the psoas muscle into the pelvic cavity. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: A patient has history contact with multiple sexual partner and develop chancre. He diagnosed as syphilis Post syphilis follow up on?
high_yield_explanation: VDRL/RPR titers are used to monitor the adequacy of syphilis treatment because they typically decline following successful penicillin therapy. A fourfold drop in titer at 6 and 12 months is the standard indicator of a successful clinical response. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Microbiology).

question_text: Tramadol mechanism of action is:
high_yield_explanation: Tramadol is a very weak mu-opioid receptor agonist that also inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin. This dual mechanism provides analgesia with a lower risk of respiratory depression compared to stronger opioids like morphine. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Pharmacology).

question_text: Loss of two points discrimination, fine touch and vibrations in the left lower limbs. The region at brain affected would be:
high_yield_explanation: The fasciculus gracilis carries fine touch and proprioception from the lower body and legs (below T6). Damage to this medial part of the posterior column leads to ipsilateral loss of these critical tactile sensations. Reference: Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy.

question_text: After hypophysectomy which cells will be affected?
high_yield_explanation: Hypophysectomy removes the source of TSH, leading to the atrophy and inactivity of the thyroid's follicular cells. In contrast, parathyroid cells and adrenal medullary cells are not primarily dependent on the anterior pituitary for their regulation. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Endocrinology).

question_text: A drug given for chronic use needs close monitoring because?
high_yield_explanation: Drugs with a low therapeutic index (e.g., Lithium, Digoxin, Warfarin) have a narrow window between their effective and toxic doses. Frequent blood level monitoring is mandatory to ensure efficacy while avoiding serious systemic toxicity. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Pharmacology).

question_text: After how much time repeat semen analysis should be done?
high_yield_explanation: The full cycle of spermatogenesis and maturation takes approximately 74 days (roughly 2.5 to 3 months). Therefore, a repeat semen analysis should be delayed for at least 2-3 months to accurately reflect any changes in sperm production. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: During hysterectomy ovarian artery damages at:
high_yield_explanation: The ovarian artery enters the pelvis within the infundibulopelvic (suspensory) ligament by crossing the pelvic brim. This location is a critical surgical 'danger zone' where the artery is often ligated and the nearby ureter must be protected. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Pelvis with anterior-posterior shorter than transverse diameter which type?
high_yield_explanation: The Android pelvis (male-like) has a heart-shaped inlet where the transverse diameter is wider than the AP diameter, and the subpubic arch is narrow. This morphology is associated with increased difficulty during labor due to poor pelvic capacity. Reference: Williams Obstetrics.

question_text: Histology of macula densa is:
high_yield_explanation: The macula densa is a specialized region of the distal convoluted tubule where the cells become tall and column-shaped (columnar). These cells act as chemoreceptors that monitor NaCl concentration to regulate GFR and renin release. Reference: Wheater's Functional Histology.

question_text: Transfer of heat from the core of the body to the surface depends on:
high_yield_explanation: Heat transfer depends on the temperature gradient between the warm body core and the skin surface. The body regulates this 'internal conduction' primarily by adjusting cutaneous blood flow via autonomic control. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Elevation of Jaw done by:
high_yield_explanation: The masseter, temporalis, and medial pterygoid muscles are responsible for elevating the mandible (closing the mouth). The lateral pterygoid is the only muscle of mastication that primarily acts to depress the jaw (open the mouth). Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy.

question_text: Child presented with Scaphocephaly and frontal bossing which is due to premature closure of which suture?
high_yield_explanation: Scaphocephaly (dolichocephaly) is the most common form of craniosynostosis, caused by the premature fusion of the sagittal suture. This forces the skull to grow longitudinally (long and narrow) because lateral expansion is restricted. Reference: Langman's Medical Embryology.

question_text: Maximum blood after transfusion will be in:
high_yield_explanation: The venous system acts as the primary blood reservoir (capacitance vessels), containing approximately 60-70% of the total blood volume at any given time. Any volume expansion from transfusion will predominantly reside in the highly distensible veins. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: A structure with ciliated and non-ciliated epithelium having three layers of muscles and tubular glands is:
high_yield_explanation: The Fallopian tube (oviduct) is lined by simple columnar ciliated cells (to move the zygote) and non-ciliated peg cells (secreting nutrients). Its wall contains a complex smooth muscle arrangement, and while it lacks true 'glands' in the lamina propria like the uterus, the peg cells function as a secretory apparatus. Reference: Wheater's Functional Histology.

question_text: External anal sphincter supplied by:
high_yield_explanation: The external anal sphincter is under voluntary somatic control and is innervated by the inferior rectal nerve, which is a branch of the pudendal nerve (S2-S4). This ensures that defecation can be consciously delayed until socially appropriate. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: Thrombolytics acts via:
high_yield_explanation: Thrombolytic agents (like tPA, Streptokinase, or Urokinase) function as plasminogen activators, converting the inactive zymogen plasminogen into the active enzyme plasmin. Plasmin then directly proteolytically cleaves the fibrin meshwork, dissolving the formed thrombus. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Pharmacology).

question_text: Female patient present with increased frequency and urgency diagnosed as UTI case microscopy shows gram negative motile rods urease positive lactose non fermenting on macconkey agar likely organism involved is:
high_yield_explanation: Proteus mirabilis is a common cause of UTI distinguished by its 'swarming' motility and urease production. Urease splits urea into ammonia, raising the urinary pH and predisposing the patient to the formation of magnesium ammonium phosphate (struvite) stones. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Microbiology).

question_text: A wave on JVP correspond to:
high_yield_explanation: The 'a wave' in the jugular venous pulse represents right atrial contraction, which occurs at the end of diastole. On an ECG, this mechanical event follows the P wave and occurs during the PR segment, just before the onset of ventricular systole. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: A young pregnant lady with the history of recurrent abortion and thrombosis, which condition is most likely suffering from?
high_yield_explanation: Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS) is a pro-thrombotic autoimmune state characterized by arterial/venous thrombosis and recurrent pregnancy loss due to placental infarctions. It is often diagnosed by the presence of lupus anticoagulant or anti-cardiolipin antibodies. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: A female is worried about a lump in her breast. She also has family history of CA breast. What is main risk factor in her?
high_yield_explanation: Mutations in the BRCA-1 gene significantly increase the lifetime risk of both breast and ovarian cancers. As a tumor suppressor gene responsible for DNA repair, its loss allows for the accumulation of mutations that lead to malignant transformation. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Genetics).

question_text: Which hormone store carbohydrate protein and fats?
high_yield_explanation: Insulin is the ultimate anabolic hormone; it promotes glycogenesis (carbs), protein synthesis (protein), and lipogenesis (fats) while inhibiting their breakdown. It essentially signals the body to 'store' energy during the fed state. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Upon autopsy, a patient was having a thrombus and line of Zahn this is seen in:
high_yield_explanation: Lines of Zahn are microscopic laminations of pale platelet/fibrin layers and darker red cell layers that only form in flowing blood. Their presence allows pathologists to definitively distinguish a pre-mortem thrombus from a post-mortem 'curd-flesh' or 'chicken-fat' clot. Reference: Robbins Basic Pathology.

question_text: Surgeon did operation to separate rectum and bladder which one separate them:
high_yield_explanation: In males, the rectovesical septum (Denonvilliers' fascia) is a thin fascial layer that separates the rectum from the bladder, prostate, and seminal vesicles. It serves as an important surgical plane and a barrier to the spread of malignancy. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: A 29-years-old female with microcytic low MCHC anemia does not fully respond to iron supplements. How will you confirm the cause of continuity of her anaemia?
high_yield_explanation: Failure to respond to iron in a microcytic anemia suggests a non-deficiency cause, most commonly Thalassemia trait. Hemoglobin electrophoresis is required to detect elevated levels of HbA2 or HbF, confirming a quantitative defect in globin chain synthesis. Reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine.

question_text: A gunshot fracture to the pterion causes an epidural hemorrhage due to involvement of which artery?
high_yield_explanation: The pterion is the thinnest part of the skull where four bones meet; the middle meningeal artery (a branch of the maxillary) runs directly deep to it. A fracture at this point typically ruptures the artery, leading to a lens-shaped epidural hematoma. Reference: Snell's Clinical Anatomy by Regions.

question_text: NK cells cause following:
high_yield_explanation: Natural Killer (NK) cells are innate immune lymphocytes that target and kill virus-infected cells and tumor cells. They recognize cells with decreased MHC Class I expression (the 'missing self' signal), which is a common evasion tactic used by intracellular pathogens. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Immunology).

question_text: Ingested Glucose is absorbed in intestinal cells by:
high_yield_explanation: Glucose is absorbed across the apical membrane of enterocytes via secondary active transport through the SGLT1 (Sodium-Glucose Linked Transporter). This process couples the movement of glucose against its gradient with the downhill flow of sodium. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: A young girl uses contact lenses, present with red, itchy, inflamed cornea. Which organism is the likely cause of her infection?
high_yield_explanation: Acanthamoeba keratitis is a serious corneal infection classically associated with poor contact lens hygiene (e.g., using tap water). This free-living amoeba can cause persistent, painful ulcers that are resistant to standard antibiotic therapy. Reference: Jawetz Medical Microbiology.

question_text: Patient presented with Macroglossia, hyperglycemia, and HTN. Which cell type's secretion is raised?
high_yield_explanation: The presentation (macroglossia, hypertension, hyperglycemia) is diagnostic of Acromegaly, caused by excessive Growth Hormone (GH) secretion from a pituitary adenoma of Somatotroph cells. GH stimulates IGF-1 production, leading to generalized soft tissue and bone overgrowth. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Endocrinology).

question_text: Which hormone maintains water and electrolytes?
high_yield_explanation: Aldosterone is the primary mineralocorticoid that regulates both sodium (electrolyte) retention and secondarily water retention to maintain extracellular fluid volume. While ADH only regulates free water, aldosterone's effect on sodium is key for systemic electrolyte balance. Reference: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology.

question_text: Trauma to the lateral side of the foot. Which lymphatics involved will be:
high_yield_explanation: Lymphatic vessels from the lateral aspect of the foot and the lateral calf travel with the small saphenous vein to drain into the popliteal lymph nodes. Most of the rest of the foot drains to the superficial inguinal nodes. Reference: Gray's Anatomy.

question_text: Hepatitis B high infectivity rate is indicated by:
high_yield_explanation: HBeAg (the 'envelope' antigen) is a direct marker of active viral replication and high infectivity. Its presence in the serum indicates that the virus is multiplying rapidly and the patient is highly likely to transmit the infection. Reference: USMLE Step 1 First Aid (Microbiology).

question_text: A girl with normal secondary sexual development with secondary amenorrhoea on USG uterus absent. Defect is in:
